reviewed_by: Automated static review in this session (Binary Ninja MCP binaryninja_ui_mcp 0.1.0: bn_function_info/bn_function_disassembly/bn_function_decompile/bn_function_basic_blocks/bn_function_callees/bn_function_callers/bn_memory_read; Radare2 6.2.0 af/agfj/pdf; angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast via scripts/angr_analyze.py) against retail igi.exe and engine/src/retail/core/retail_error.cpp
scope: Source-semantic and control-flow review of retail Debug_Error (0x004AF7B0) against the C++ implementation in engine/src/retail/core/retail_error.cpp. Retail-image structure is established by Binary Ninja, Radare2 CFG and angr CFGFast. No differential runner or runtime capture covers this translation unit; behavioral equivalence is not claimed.

decompiler.prototype_note: Binary Ninja reports a non-variadic one-argument prototype. The 274 retail call sites clean 4, 8 or more stack bytes after the call (for example 0x00415B6A add esp,8 and 0x00415F8D add esp,4), and 0x004A53B3 is the variadic sprintf wrapper, so the reviewed cdecl variadic signature is the ABI the call sites prove. This is a reviewed ABI adaptation, not an exact-prototype match.

retail_structure.byte_binding: bn_memory_read(0x004AF7B0, 89) returned exactly these bytes; the sha256 above is computed from that byte string.

abi.return_value: EAX; 0 on the null exit-callback path, otherwise the exit callback's return value forwarded by `jmp eax`
abi.stack_cleanup: caller (274 call sites, e.g. 0x00415B6A add esp,8; 0x00415F8D add esp,4)

branch_semantics: 0x004AF7B0: mov eax,[0x00936268]; test eax,eax; je 0x004AF7FD - report block is entered only when the display callback is non-null.

0x004AF7B9-0x004AF7FC: push edi; sprintf(0x00A84640, "Fatal error:\n\n"); scan 0x00A84640 with repne scasb; String_VFormat(0x00A84640 + strlen, format, varargs); g_936268(0x00A84640); add esp,0x18; pop edi.
0x004AF7FD: mov eax,[0x0093626C]; test eax,eax; je 0x004AF808 - null exit callback returns 0.
0x004AF806: jmp eax - non-null exit callback is tail-dispatched and its result is the caller-visible result.

0x004AF808: retn - the raw entry has a genuine return path; this is confirmed independently by Binary Ninja's decompiler (`return 93626c_1;` where 93626c_1 is 0), Radare2 (one retn) and angr (function reported returning).

callees.role: sprintf(char* buffer, const char* format, ...) CRT wrapper
String_VFormat(char* buffer, const char* format, va_list args) CRT vsprintf wrapper

globals.role: fatal message buffer written by sprintf and appended to by String_VFormat

callback_context: 0x00498900 installs all four error callbacks. The two read here are set to 0x004988D0 (display) and 0x00498930 (exit).
0x004988D0 is a MessageBoxA wrapper: ShowCursor(1); MessageBoxA(hWnd, buffer, caption, 0x10 /* MB_ICONHAND */); ShowCursor(0). Retail performs no file or console logging in this path.

0x00498930 calls 0x0048F1B0; when that reports the process is debugged it calls the DebugBreak import, then pushes 1 and calls the CRT exit wrapper 0x004A5AD5. 0x004A5AD5 calls 0x004A5AF7(1, 0, 0); 0x004A5AF7 calls ExitProcess(1) (or TerminateProcess(GetCurrentProcess(), 1) when g_9360AC == 1). That path does not return.
Both callbacks are zero in the file image, so before 0x00498900 runs the raw entry reports nothing and returns 0.

radare2_cross_check.cfg_identity: Node and edge identity matches the Binary Ninja graph exactly (gate score 1.0).

angr_cfgfast.note: The automatic CFGFast baseline leaves the indirect `jmp eax` unresolved. The helper validates the retail initializer bytes (0x00498900 pushes 0x00498930 and calls setter 0x004AF8A0, which stores it into 0x0093626C) before modelling that one concrete callback, after which no jumps are unresolved. The 10 blocks are CFGFast's instruction-level splits of the same 5-block function; they are not a boundary disagreement.

compile_check.object_function_shape: The Debug_Error function has two conditional callback guards, 6 call sites (Error_GetGlobals, sprintf, strlen, String_VFormat, display callback, exit callback) and 2 return instructions. The previous unconditional self-loop and the missing return path are gone.

control_flow: guard 1: if (globals.g_936268 != nullptr) - same display-callback gate as retail.

report block: error::sprintf(g_a84640, "Fatal error:\n\n"); NUL scan; error::String_VFormat(g_a84640 + prefix_length, format, arguments); globals.g_936268(g_a84640); - same call order, buffer and arguments as retail.
guard 2: exit_callback = globals.g_93626c; if (exit_callback == nullptr) return 0; - same null test and EAX=0 result as retail 0x004AF7FD/0x004AF808.
non-null exit path: return exit_callback(); - returns the callback's result to the caller, matching the `jmp eax` tail dispatch at 0x004AF806.
There is no self-loop in the function; the terminal fatal-call contract lives in the retail callers' `jmp $` and in the candidate callers' halt_forever().
candidate_structure.storage: Retail globals 0x00936268, 0x0093626C and 0x00A84640 are represented by ErrorGlobalsState fields g_936268, g_93626c and g_a84640, reached through Error_GetGlobals() and shared with engine/src/retail/error/error_show.cpp.

comparison.identity: The candidate implements the single retail entry at 0x004AF7B0; Binary Ninja and Radare2 agree on that entry and on the 5-block/5-edge graph.
comparison.signature: Both are x86 cdecl variadic int32_t(const char* format, ...); the first stack word is the format and the remaining stack words are substitutions.
comparison.branches: Both have two conditional gates: display callback non-null and exit callback non-null. The fall-through/report path and both exit outcomes line up with the retail blocks 0x004AF7B0/0x004AF7B9/0x004AF7FD/0x004AF806/0x004AF808.
comparison.report_sequence: Both call the sprintf role first, scan the NUL, append with the String_VFormat/vsprintf role at that offset, then call the display callback with 0x00A84640.
comparison.return_contract: Both return 0 when the exit callback is null and otherwise expose the exit callback's result. Retail tail-jumps (`jmp eax`); the candidate calls and returns. The stack state at dispatch is the same because the arguments were already cleaned and the caller cleans the variadic arguments (cdecl).
comparison.side_effects: The only side effects are the shared buffer write, the display callback call and the exit callback call. The candidate adds none.
comparison.cfg_score_scope: The record's cfg_similarity 1.0 is Binary Ninja versus Radare2 agreement on the retail image, not a candidate-versus-retail machine-CFG score.

resolved_divergences: Previous revision: when 0x0093626C was null the candidate entered `for (;;)` instead of returning 0. Retail 0x004AF808 is a retn with EAX already zero; the review found this as a genuine control-flow divergence and the implementation now returns 0.
Previous revision: the exit callback was called for effect and the self-loop discarded its return value. Retail's `jmp eax` forwards the callback result; the candidate now returns it.

Previous revision: the function added a self-loop to stand in for the retail callers' `jmp $`. That contract is already enforced at the candidate call sites (terrain_quadtree.cpp calls halt_forever() after Debug_Error), so the self-loop was removed rather than kept as a local deviation.

divergences.detail: Retail tail-dispatches the exit callback with `jmp eax`; the candidate emits `call *%eax; ...; ret`. Both return to Debug_Error's caller with the callback's EAX value. If the installed callback is noreturn (0x00498930 -> exit(1) -> ExitProcess(1)) both paths terminate identically.

Retail addresses 0x00936268/0x0093626C/0x00A84640 directly. The candidate reads the same three fields through Error_GetGlobals(), a port-owned ErrorGlobalsState shared with Error_Show (the same retail VA). Field order and roles match; the absolute addresses are not reproduced.

Retail scans the buffer with an inline `repne scasb` (0xFFFFFFFF bound). GCC recognizes the candidate's NUL loop and emits a `strlen` call. For a NUL-terminated buffer the resulting offset is identical; the retail scan's 0xFFFFFFFF bound is unreachable for a real C string.

The sprintf (0x004A53B3) and String_VFormat (0x004A5702) calls are satisfied by the port wrappers in error_show.cpp, which delegate to the MinGW CRT vsprintf. The call order, buffer pointer arithmetic and arguments match; the candidate does not reimplement the retail CRT internals in this translation unit.

limitations: No runtime or behavioral evidence exists for this translation unit. The review is static (Binary Ninja, Radare2, angr) plus a compile check; it does not claim runtime equivalence.

The candidate installs neither callback global. Retail installs g_936268=0x004988D0 and g_93626C=0x00498930 at 0x00498900. Until those installations are ported, the candidate's runtime path takes the null-exit-callback branch: it is silent and returns 0, with no message box and no process exit.
The installed callbacks are outside this translation unit and remain unported: 0x004988D0 (MessageBoxA with MB_ICONHAND) and 0x00498930 (DebugBreak when debugged, then CRT exit(1) -> ExitProcess(1)).

A caller that ignores the fatal contract could resume after Debug_Error in the candidate when both callbacks are null; retail's examined callers append `jmp $`, and the candidate call sites in terrain_quadtree.cpp append halt_forever(). Callers not examined here are outside the scope of this review.

The CFG score recorded with the native is the retail Binary Ninja-vs-Radare2 score (1.0). No candidate machine-CFG similarity is claimed; the candidate's call-plus-return exit path is a reviewed equivalence, not an address-identical tail jump.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja (5 blocks, 5 edges, 89 bytes, 29 instructions) and Radare2 (5 blocks, 5 edges, 89 bytes, 29 instructions) recover one function at 0x004AF7B0 with identical node/edge identity; angr CFGFast recovers the exact entry with no unresolved jumps once the retail initializer's concrete exit callback is modelled. The candidate implements that entry.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: The first stack argument is the printf-style format, followed by variadic substitutions. The candidate keeps `const char* format, ...` under extern "C" x86 cdecl. The 274 call sites clean 4/8/... bytes themselves, which proves caller cleanup; Binary Ninja's non-variadic prototype is a decompiler simplification documented in the record's signature comparison.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The literal "Fatal error:\n\n" is at 0x00546DB8, the destination buffer is 0x00A84640, and the append offset is derived by scanning for its first NUL. The candidate uses the same literal and buffer field and computes the same offset; no other constants or scaling factors exist in the function.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail reads 4-byte callback pointers from 0x00936268/0x0093626C and writes a byte string at 0x00A84640. The candidate's ErrorGlobalsState exposes the same three fields with the same roles and sizes through Error_GetGlobals(); the absolute addresses are replaced by port-owned storage, which is the documented adaptation.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Both call the sprintf role (0x004A53B3), the String_VFormat/vsprintf role (0x004A5702), then g_936268(0x00A84640), and finally dispatch g_93626C. The candidate adds no side effect. The only state change is the shared message buffer, as in retail.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail has two outcomes after the report: null exit callback -> retn with EAX=0, non-null -> jmp eax forwarding the callback result. The candidate now has exactly those two outcomes (`return 0;` and `return exit_callback();`). The previous unconditional self-loop was removed because it removed the retail return path; no other branch is simplified away.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Neither the retail body nor the candidate performs floating-point arithmetic; the function only tests pointers, copies a literal and formats a C string.
